scope: Blind output assessment of ten fresh intake replies with supplied drafts and tool-call records; not a branch review or formal closing-review gate verdict. No source, plans, other audits or additional model calls consulted.
limits: No global dogfood pass is asserted.
Reference-reading flags are observations only, not pass/fail prerequisites.
No mandatory headings, word counts or arbitrary length cap applied. Brevity/proportionality is assessed as an explicit user outcome, separately from material fidelity.
Known missing facts and pending interviews are valid; absence of a draft or completed confirmation is not alone a failure.
No disclosure requirement imposed before an actual yes question. When yes is asked, assess informed same-yes publication, opt-out and separate merge.

Recorded calls show inspection/repair and open-draft writing, with no recorded confirmed-state write, git commit, push or PR creation. This is bounded packet evidence, not complete live-state attestation.

cases.stage: Pending date interview plus conditional yes request; no draft is not itself a failure.
cases.basis: Explains document, old-date impact, date-only correction and acceptance; keeps replacement unknown. Asking yes includes branch publication, opt-out and separate merge consequences. No premature confirmation, commit or publication is recorded.

findings.consequence: Job-owned rule isolation does not imply the rule always selects the same worker. Asking the user whether to retain this extra proposed acceptance criterion creates an unnecessary quality decision and risks expanding scope to determinism. The later invitation to delete it mitigates finalization risk but does not make the extra decision necessary. A legitimate pending interview about observed examples or unknown cause remains valid.

findings.consequence: For a verified one-command correction, the reply adds unexplained contract/standing-document diagnostics, classification and next-station mechanics after already giving the scope and authorization. These details require extra reading without helping the user decide the requested correction. Necessary publication disclosure is not the source of this finding.
